tb-406-1.question:
The structure of a d.c. motor is shown in Figure a. The motor consists of two parts: the electromagnet and the rotator (coil Y).

Which of the following actions can reverse the direction of rotation of coil Y?

(1) Reverse the polarity of cell P.

(2) Reverse the polarity of cell Q.

(3) Reverse the polarity of both cells P and Q.

A (1) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-406-1.reasoning:
(1): The magnetic field produced by coil X, hence the magnetic field experienced by coil Y, is reversed. Therefore, the torque acting on coil Y is reversed.

∴ (1) is correct.

(2): The current in coil Y is reversed. Therefore, the torque acting on coil Y is reversed.

∴ (2) is correct.

(3): Both the magnetic field experienced by coil Y and the current in coil Y are reversed. Therefore, the torque acting on coil Y does not change its direction.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-406-2.question:
An electron enters a uniform magnetic field. Its direction of motion makes an angle larger than 0° with the magnetic field. Which of the following statements about the electron is/are correct?

(1) The kinetic energy of the electron remains unchanged.

(2) It continues to travel with acceleration.

(3) Its direction of motion will eventually become perpendicular to the magnetic field.

A (2) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1) and (3) only
tb-406-2.reasoning:
The magnetic field applies a force on the electron perpendicular to its motion, so it accelerates but has no change in kinetic energy.

∴ (1) and (2) are correct.

Since the magnetic force is always perpendicular to the magnetic field, the component of the electron’s velocity along the magnetic field will never change and thus its direction of motion will not become perpendicular to the field.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-406-8.question:
Figure f shows a charged particle P moving in a region with electric field E and magnetic field B mutually perpendicular to each other. At the instant shown, P is moving with a velocity v which is perpendicular to both fields. The dotted line shows its path afterwards.

Which of the following about P must be correct?

(1) P is negatively charged.

(2) The kinetic energy of P increases when it travels in the fields.

(3) v≠EB

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-406-8.reasoning:
If the charge is positive, both the electric and magnetic force point upwards. If the charge is negative, both forces point downwards.

∴ (1) is correct.

The magnetic force is always perpendicular to its motion, so there is no work done by magnetic force.

However, there is work done by the electric force as the motion of P has a vertical component pointing downwards.

∴ (2) is correct.

v =EBis the criterion when the electric force and magnetic force cancel out each other. However, in this setup, the electric force and magnetic force point in the same direction. This gives no information about v.

∴ (3) is not necessarily correct.

tb-406-9.question:
A charged particle moves in a straight line when passing through a uniform magnetic field between two parallel charged plates (Fig g).

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The particle must deflect upwards if it carries the opposite charge.

(2) The particle must deflect downwards if it moves at a lower speed.

(3) The upper plate must be the positive plate.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-406-9.reasoning:
The magnetic force and the electrostatic force balance each other.

Regardless of whether X carry positive or negative charge, the magnetic force and electric force are in opposite directions and still cancel out each other. The particle would still pass through the region in a straight line.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

If the particle moves at a lower speed, the magnetic force will be smaller. The particle will deflect downwards if it carries positive charge, and deflect upwards if it carries negative charge.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

The electric field must point downwards so that the electric force and the magnetic force are in opposite direction. So, the upper plate must be positive.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-406-10.question:
A student sets up a motor as shown (Fig h). Solenoids X, Y and coil PQRS are connected to the same power supply.

Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) If a d.c. power supply is used, the coil will rotate clockwise when observed from point Z.

(2) If an a.c. power supply is used, the coil will only oscillate.

(3) The coil will rotate faster if X and Y have more turns per unit length.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-406-10.reasoning:
Depending on the polarity of the power supply, the following may occur:

The magnetic field points to the right and the current in the coil flows from S to P, or

the magnetic field points to the left and the current in the coil flows from P to S.

In both cases, the coil will rotate clockwise.

∴ (1) is correct.

The coil will rotate clockwise regardless of the polarity of the power supply.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

If X and Y have more turns per unit length, the coil will experience a stronger magnetic field. Therefore, the moment acting on the coil will become stronger.

∴ (3) is correct.
